caveats: life-t's folder is ibm_kingston-2026-10-14-life-t-legacy (run 1's SamplerV2, untwirled, IBM's classified readout).
IBM's T1 and T2 were the same in every calibration from 20:27 to 22:23 (only readout changed), so 'IBM's values in force' for life-t are also the ones Exp 1's model took.

Hahn T2 was echoed on all 65 qubits at once, so ZZ between neighbours is not refocused. Our T2 is 0.31 of IBM's (median) and not exponential: IBM's T2 times exp(-(t/tau)^2), tau ~ 59 us, fits 60 of 65 qubits better (median chi2/dof 1.15 against 3.17). It levels off near 45-50 us whatever IBM's value: 0.23 of IBM's where IBM's is above 120 us, 0.65 where it is below 50 us. That is what one added dephasing, the same on every qubit, would do. A few points dip below 1/2 (7 of 65 at 132 us beyond 2 sigma, ~1.5 expected), as coherent ZZ would make them; as ZZ it needs ~7.6 kHz rms per qubit. Under XY4 in the circuit, Exp 1's T_q is 0.74 of IBM's T2 (median), about 3 times our Hahn T2. So life-t's T2 reads as an artifact of echoing everything at once, not as IBM overstating T2, and no model uses it.
T1 at one time vs IBM's at another: T1 drifts (TLS), so >3 sigma differences on single qubits are expected even with both correct; the median agrees.

In situ, only each test's decay per round is measured well. The two tests split T1 from T_q with correlation near -1. Unbounded, 1/T_phi < 0 for 14 of 25 qubits (beyond 2 sigma for 7), 1/T_q < 0 for 8 and 1/T1 < 0 for 3. So 17 of 25 sit on a bound of the model's region (14 at T_q = 2 T1, 3 at T1 = inf). There the bounded fit cannot give the test read in Z all its decay: the sum over data is 11% short, while the test read in X gets 3% too much.

So the in-situ model (analysis.in_situ's bounded values) moves O/M partly for the wrong reason, and its result depends on the split: moving all data qubits together 1 sigma along the degeneracy (1/T1 up) gives X eps +18-25% and Z +15-16%; the other way gives X +2-7% and Z -2 to -3%. The asymmetry comes mostly from the bound. The 'matched' variant uses only what is measured: each memory at its own test's decay per round. Two different splits of it agree to within 2% per eps, so the model depends on the decay per round, not on the split.

The Z test decays more along Z than T_q <= 2 T1 allows, given the X test. With life-t's T1 near IBM's for the data (median 0.98 over the data), the excess is not plain T1 but something in the circuit acting on Z-axis states, e.g. pulse errors beyond the model's depolarizing, leakage, or neighbours' readout.
Observed eps are decoded on Exp 1's measured-T_q model (as analysis.exp1 does). Decoding on the in-situ model instead raises observed eps by 0.4-1.6%.

The model takes 20:27's readout, as Exp 1's O/M did. That calibration puts data 72 and 12 at ~20% readout error, against ~5% during the jobs. With 21:55's readout the model's eps fall, and O/M rises: at measured T_q to X 1.68/1.82 and Z 1.33/1.28; matched, to X 1.68/1.80 and Z 1.05/1.12.
Model: 200k shots per circuit, seed 0, cap 0.1 only. The model's eps error is dominated by the curve-shape dispersion at d=3 (binomial dispersion ~12-15), not by the shots.
